narrator.how: a storyteller in the tone of Saint-Exupéry: quiet, clear and unhurried, grave and lyrical at once; speaks seldom, and when he does, of the sky, the lights below and what men pay — with a restrained, luminous sadness

riviere.how: the director of the night mail, past fifty: low, dry, even and short; speaks in orders, never explains, never raises his voice; when something touches him he grows colder and shorter, and the pause before a word is longer

fabien.how: a pilot of thirty, married six weeks: calm, precise, a little warm, no bravado; few words, as written on a note in the air

madame.how: a young wife of twenty-two: soft, quiet and polite, apologising for being in the way; holds herself together, never cries out, never accuses; asks about him, not about herself

robineau.how: the inspector: a lonely, fussy, timid man who loves his reports; hesitant, starts sentences and does not finish them, clears his throat; afraid of the director and fond of him

pellerin.how: a mail pilot just down after crossing the Andes in a storm: offhand and laughing, plays it down for the mechanics; under the joke, a tremor he hides

roblet.how: an old mechanic, twenty years on the engines: hoarse, slow and simple, ashamed; asks once and falls silent

radioman.how: Fabien's young radio operator: a few words read from a note, clipped, over the engine's roar

telegraphist.how: the telegraphist: an even, flat voice reading the reports off the tape, as he has read every report for twenty years; never a private word

pilot.how: the European mail's pilot: young, firm and spare with words; asks for nothing; standing on the ground by a ready plane is the worst thing for him

asuncion.how: the Asunción mail's pilot, just down on time: plain, a little tired, an ordinary working man's voice

mechanic.how: a young mechanic of the field: quick, plain, a little unsure before the director

mechanic_b.how: an older mechanic of the field: stocky, slow, says little

mechanic_c.how: a lanky mechanic of the field: quiet
